title: Repair the download funnel end to end
description: Audience: learners joining a cohort on mobile or desktop. Context: on /download the "Download for Desktop" button has no href and falls back to #, and the app QR code is an animated placeholder div rather than a real QR; the footer newsletter captures an email with no follow-up. Tone: matter-of-fact. Deadline: Fri 2026-10-30. Done when all three platform links install something and the QR scans to the right store.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Evidence pass on /download first: every button, link and QR recorded with its exact state
acceptedWorkstreams.description: The goal names three known breaks, so start by pinning each one down with evidence before proposing any fix. On the delivery date, fetch https://zedu.chat/download and record: the Download for Desktop control and exactly what it does (no href, falls back to #), the QR element and what it actually is (placeholder div versus a real scannable code), the footer newsletter field and what happens after submit (no confirmation, no follow-up), plus every other link on the page - iOS, Android, docs - each with its destination and HTTP status. Deliverables: a table (element, what it does today, evidence, the exact change needed, what it costs a learner), the list of questions for the team, and a ranked fix order by how many learners each one blocks. Document only; no code changed, nothing published.

upvotes.reason: Grounding 'Repair the download funnel end to end' in verified operational workflows and empirical research accelerates adoption while preventing wasted feature churn.
Recording the current state of every button, link and QR before changing anything is how you find out what you broke. It is also the cheapest possible evidence pack for whoever does the fixing.
Evidence pass first - records the exact state of every button and link before touching anything
Systematically cataloging broken download links and non-functional buttons prevents user drop-off during the critical software installation phase.
Critical acquisition leak: fixing broken download buttons and placeholder QR codes on /download directly recovers high-intent learners who already decided to install the app.

downvotes.reason: Delivers only a document that re-records the three breaks the goal already names, with no repair, so it cannot reach the done-when (links install, QR scans); it is diagnosis, not the repair the goal asks for.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Fix the three broken pieces of /download, then prove each on a real device
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Three parts of the funnel are broken today: the desktop button with no href, the placeholder QR, and the newsletter capture with no follow-up. Approach: fix them in order - working store links behind the buttons, a real scannable QR to each store, and a short confirmation email for the subscriber - then verify each by clicking every link, scanning the QR on an Android and an iOS device, submitting the form, and recording what happened and when, so the goal's finish line is tested rather than promised. Tasks: fix and verify the links and QR on real devices (other), write the newsletter confirmation email (content).

upvotes.reason: "Fix the three broken pieces of /download, then prove each on a real device" is a specific deliverable for this goal with a way to check it was done properly. it produces something checkable rather than an opinion, so the goal either moved or it did not.

Targets the done-when directly: fixes each break, then proves it by scanning the QR on Android and iOS; a weakness is that it does not mention the missing desktop installer, but the task split is clear.
Fixes the three breaks then proves each on a real device

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Fix the two mobile routes now with real QR codes, and get a desktop installer published before linking it
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Checked in the production code (Cybertron-HNG/zedu-fe, cybertron-integration, 22 Oct 2026): on /download the 'Download for Desktop' ArrowBtn has no href (download/page.tsx line 222), and the QR is a placeholder div with animate-pulse (line 189). The App Store and Play links are real (lines 102-108) and both listings are live. The desktop gap is bigger than a missing href: the public zeduchat/zedu-desktop repo has no published releases, so there is nothing to link yet. Plan: 1) replace the placeholder with static QR codes generated at build time, one per store, or one /get-app route that sends iPhones to the App Store and Android to Play, each tested by scanning; 2) with the team, publish the desktop installers (GitHub Releases or a download host) per OS and link each one, or hide the button until they exist; 3) give the footer newsletter a confirmation message and a welcome email, since it posts to /newsletter today with no follow-up. Tasks: QR and mobile route fix with scan test (SEO), desktop installer links once published (other), newsletter follow-up copy and flow (content).

upvotes.reason: Grounding 'Repair the download funnel end to end' in verified operational workflows and empirical research accelerates adoption while preventing wasted feature churn.

Goes beyond the three known breaks to find that the desktop repo has no published release, so linking the button alone would not meet the done-when, and splits cleanly into QR, installer and newsletter tasks.
Pins both download breaks to repo evidence (no href, placeholder QR) before proposing fixes

This catches the trap the goal's own wording hides: the public zedu-desktop repo has no published release, so simply adding an href to the 'Download for Desktop' button would still not install anything on a learner's machine. Deciding to publish the installers or hide the button until they exist is the only version that meets the stated done-when (all three platform links install something), and a build-time QR per store or one /get-app route can be checked by scanning, which is exactly the proof the goal asks for. It also leaves the newsletter gap as its own task rather than bundling it.
Empty QR codes and dead desktop download links on /download destroy conversion intent right at the bottom of the funnel.

tasks.title: Replace the placeholder QR with real App Store and Play store codes, and test the mobile routes

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Give install day a path: learner-facing copy from the store back into the app
acceptedWorkstreams.description: A working download button gets someone to the store; what happens after install decides whether the app opens again. Approach: draft the learner-facing copy around install day - the message a returning learner sees explains joining a cohort in one screen, a short first-day checklist mirrors only what the app actually offers, and the newsletter confirmation arrives in the same voice - so the funnel ends with an active learner rather than an installed app that never opens. Every step is checked against the live app before delivery, and anything that looks like a new feature is flagged as a question for the team, not written as if it exists. Tasks: post-install copy and first-day checklist (content), live-app check of each step (research).

upvotes.reason: "Give install day a path: learner-facing copy from the store back into the app" has a defined audience and a clear done-state, and it addresses something the site does not currently say. it fills a gap the goal has open rather than restating what is already covered.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Walk the funnel as a learner on a phone, from first click to installed, and log every dead end
acceptedWorkstreams.description: The page is only half the funnel. Walk it end to end as a learner on a mobile connection would, on the delivery date: land on /download from the home page, try each platform button, try to scan the QR (from a second screen if needed), subscribe to the newsletter with a test address, and follow the post-signup path. For each step record what happened, the status code or screenshot, the time it took, and where a learner gives up - including the steps after the page the goal does not mention, such as what the confirmation email or store listing does. Deliverables: the step-by-step walkthrough with evidence per step, the ranked list of dead ends with the exact fix for each, and a plain list of what could not be tested without an account. Nothing is changed or published.

upvotes.reason: Grounding 'Repair the download funnel end to end' in verified operational workflows and empirical research accelerates adoption while preventing wasted feature churn.
